thread:
Iris: Quick alert 1: customers hit TLS errors in ap-south after yesterday's KMS key policy change that scoped decrypt to a specific principal. Seeing `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` in svc logs.
Devon: can you paste the earliest error?
Iris: `2026-03-24T11:03:07Z cert-issuer: failed to unwrap key: AccessDeniedException: Not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt on key arn:aws:kms:ap-south-1:.../rotator-key` then `grpc: failed to create client transport: connection error: desc = "transport: authentication handshake failed: remote error: tls: bad certificate"`
Maya: sounds like the private key wasn't available so new cert couldn't be issued; services tried to use an untrusted cert. did the key move to HSM-backed key?
Iris: yes - policy tightened and we also rotated to multi-tenant HSM key for stronger audit. But the binding didn't include the cert-issuer's node role in ap-south.
Devon: audit-bot, pull CloudTrail KMS denies and the assumed-role ARNs for that window.
audit-bot: CloudTrail entries: 6 denies between 11:02:50 and 11:05:10 UTC. Principals show `arn:aws:sts::123:assumed-role/cert-issuer-ap-south/i-0abc1234` and `arn:aws:sts::123:assumed-role/cert-rotator-ap-south/cert-rotator-5c7b`
Maya: interesting 1: cert-issuer runs on nodes with instance role `cert-issuer-ap-south`, but rotator runs as a k8s SA `cert-rotator`. Key policy allowed the SA but not the instance role.
Iris: mitigation idea: update key policy to allow both principals and add `kms:ViaService` condition for kms.amazonaws.com from ap-south. Also add `sts:TagSession` requirement so session tags show kube namespace/pod.
Devon: short-term patch: attach an IAM policy granting kms:Decrypt to the instance role cert-issuer-ap-south. long-term: canonicalize mapping in `infra/iam/region-mappings.yaml`.
Maya: also saw ocsp stapling failures in logs: `OCSP: no response` after cert reissue attempts. Could be because our OCSP responder uses a cert that wasn't reissued due to same KMS issue. That amplifies client trust failures.
Iris: good catch. escalate to infra-oncall: we need to ensure OCSP responder keys are untouched and reachable.
infra-oncall: on it. I'll open a short maintenance window for ap-south, add the instance role to the KMS keypolicy and restart the cert-issuer service.
Devon: before doing changes, snapshot current key policy and IAM state: `aws kms get-key-policy --key-id alias/rotator-key --policy-name default > /tmp/rotator-policy.json` and `aws iam get-role --role-name cert-issuer-ap-south` then upload to `s3://sec-incident-archive/4987659999/`.
Iris: we should also instrument our cert-agent to emit `sts:GetCallerIdentity` and the KMS key id on every unwrap attempt to make future correlation easier.
Maya: and add a small agent-side circuit-breaker: if decrypt fails N times in M minutes, fall back to prior key cache for a grace period to avoid mass handshake failures. Documented in `runbooks/keystore-fallback.md`.
Devon: infra-oncall update: added role to key policy at 11:22:40 UTC and restarted services at 11:25:05. OCSP responder validated at 11:29:13.
Iris: after restart we see `unwrap succeeded` and cert issuance completes. Grepping service logs show no `bad certificate` after 11:30.
Maya: follow-ups: 1) set CloudTrail retention in ap-south to 180 days for compliance investigations; 2) require `sts:TagSession` for all KMS clients and update libraries to set `KMS_SESSION_TAGS` (namespace,pod,job); 3) review TLS profiles: enforce TLS1.3 for inter-region control-plane traffic and block CBC/RC4 ciphers; 4) add automated policy-linting that fails PRs that tighten key policies without a footprint check.
Devon: opened ticket SEC-789 to track the automation and retention changes. Assigned to Security Infra.
Iris: root cause summary in incident doc: 1) key-policy scoping change omitted instance role used by cert-issuer, 2) OCSP responder dependency created a blast radius when cert issuance failed, 3) audit telemetry lacked pod-level tags. Remediation plan: policy fix, session-tagging rollout, keystore client circuit-breaker, CI linting rule.
Maya: also flag for vuln triage: a new CVE reported in `libcerts` (CVE-2026-9999) affecting our older cert-issuer version that mishandles malformed OCSP responses. Please add to the incident follow-up and ensure we upgrade to a patched cert-issuer image.
infra-oncall: acknowledging CVE. Will schedule emergency image bump for cert-issuer and rotator in ap-south.
Devon: closing incident channel; please add any additional logs to `s3://sec-incident-archive/4987659999/` and update the incident doc with exact timeline.
Iris: thanks all. We'll take the TLS profile hardening RFC to the security weekly for approval.
